# The dock Workspace composes its default cross-window Participation

## Context

Institution #382 (→ PR neomjs/neo-agent-institution#383) measured the Fleet Manager cockpit showing no drop zones while a tab header is dragged: the cockpit extends `Neo.dashboard.dock.Workspace` with `enableDockTearOutLifecycle: true` and never composed the engine's drop-feedback tier — the façade leaves that tier to the consumer by design. Fixing it raised the question the record's author answered as its author (@neo-fable-clio, A2A 2026-10-01 12:40Z; her turn 12:41Z): should a workspace that opts into the tear-out lifecycle compose its default cross-window `Participation` itself, the way the flag already composes the tear-out machine and the maximize affordance? Yes — as its own engine leaf under #15239, with the §2.3 amendment, not inside #382. This is that leaf; PR neomjs/neo-agent-institution#383's Deltas and #382's Out of Scope name it as the follow-up.

## The Problem

Every workspace that participates in cross-window drags composes `Neo.dashboard.dock.window.Participation` by hand, and each one re-derives the same lifecycle the façade already owns the inputs of:

- `apps/workstation/view/PopupWorkspace.mjs:85-95` `syncParticipation()` — the minimal composition (`dragEmbodiment`, `hitTest`, `sortGroup`, `windowId`, `workspace`, `workspaceId`, `workspaceSet`), re-run from `afterSetWindowId` (`:77`) and after the set registration (`:67`), destroyed at `:192`.
- `apps/workstation/view/VesselWorkspace.mjs:184-195` (a `Map` + a promise), `:312-316` (construct), `:529-594` (`createCrossWindowParticipation` / `refreshCrossWindowParticipation`), `:1737-1738` (destroy) — the main workspace's composition of its `Workstation.window.Participation` subclass (`apps/workstation/window/Participation.mjs`: the saved-home drop policy) with the park / conversion seams; the class comment at `:306-312` spells out the registration triggers the app re-derives: construction when the Group is already bound, `afterSetTopologyGroupId` when a first boot's identity arrives later.
- `examples/dashboard/crossWindow/DemoBCrossWindowStage.mjs:163-215` — per projected host, with hand seams (its holder `DemoBWorkspace` extends `Container`, not the façade).
- The cockpit composes none, and its vessels are shells, so the gap there is only the missing default.

The engine class already carries a complete default for every seam when it is given its workspace: `defaultCommitLocal` (`src/dashboard/dock/window/Participation.mjs:436`), `defaultCommitTransfer` (`:456`), `defaultGetDocument` (`:479`), `defaultGetForeignDocument` (`:490`), `defaultHitTest` (`:502`), `defaultPreviewFor` (`:522`), `defaultSortGroup` (`:635` — the workspace's published `crossWindowSortGroup`; absent, "the target never registers and the workspace stays fully in-window — the unchanged opt-in default"), `defaultResolveOwnershipId` (`:654` — the workspace's Group, read live), and `resolveAffordances` (`:310` — Preview + DropIndicators + DragAffordances composed over `workspace.getDockHost()` when no controller is supplied). The one thing the engine does not own is *when* the instance exists.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs` is a façade: "it owns cross-concern ordering and the one mutation boundary, and it owns no concern outright … declinable stateful affordances, the tear-out gesture machine, multi-window lifecycle — belongs to a named owner beside it" (class doc `:91-95`). It composes two named owners today: the maximize affordance as a declinable collaborator (`:616-620` — installed unless the consumer supplied its own instance through `plugins`) and, under `enableDockTearOutLifecycle`, the tear-out handlers (`:622-657`).
- The lifecycle inputs a participation needs are façade-owned already: `windowId` (`afterSetWindowId` `:1804`, which also resolves the Group), the Group (`onTopologyGroupBinding` `:806`, `afterSetTopologyGroupId` `:969` — an empty hook whose doc says "A host whose participants could not register at construction … registers them here"), `workspaceSet` (injected before construction, `:899`), the set identity (`workspaceKey`, `:2584`), the dock host (`getDockHost()` `:1562`), teardown (`destroy()` `:1510`).
- `Neo.dashboard.dock.window.DragTarget` registers with the coordinator only while `sortGroup && windowId != null` (`src/dashboard/dock/window/DragTarget.mjs:218`, `:482`); the participation registers it at construct with `stableTargetId = workspaceId` (`Participation.mjs:273-305`), so a re-sync on a window change is destroy + recreate, never a second slot. Ordinary commits retain the same target (`test/playwright/unit/apps/workstation/Workspace.spec.mjs:132-144`).
- ADR 0029 §2.3 "Dock participation: remote drag → preview → operation" (`learn/agentos/decisions/0029-docking-design.md:351-353`) states what a dock workspace registers and which pipeline its drop rides; it does not say who composes the participation or when it exists. That is the gap the amendment closes.

## The Fix

*Corrected while building (2026-10-01 16:4xZ, the author): the opt-in is the published `crossWindowSortGroup`, not the tear-out flag — the Workstation's popup workspaces participate with `enableDockTearOutLifecycle` off (they return through their close policy), and the engine class already states the sort group as its registry identity. Every "under the tear-out lifecycle" below reads "for a published sort group"; the Institution cockpit publishes none and still composes nothing.*

1. **The façade composes the default.** For a published `crossWindowSortGroup`, `Neo.dashboard.dock.Workspace` owns one `Neo.dashboard.dock.window.Participation` bound to itself — `workspace: this`, `windowId`, `workspaceId: this.workspaceKey`, `workspaceSet`, the published `crossWindowSortGroup` through the engine default — created once the workspace has a window and publishes the sort group — the Group is read live at claim time, never waited for; the set is bound when present and re-bound when it arrives — at the construct tail, in `afterSetWindowId` (configs applied) and after `afterRefreshDockWorkspace`; a changed binding re-composes an instance the façade owns (destroy + recreate); destroyed in `destroy()` before the tear-out handlers retire *(sentence corrected 2026-10-01 18:1xZ on @neo-gpt-sophie's second read; the first version named the Group, the set and `afterSetTopologyGroupId`)*. A workspace that publishes no `crossWindowSortGroup` composes nothing — the opt-in default the engine class already states; the tear-out flag plays no part.
2. **Declinable, the maximize way.** One config, `dockParticipation`, following the `dockHeaderActionPolicy` instance-or-config shape (`:1535`): the default is `true` (the engine class, imported on first use); `null` declines (a consumer keeping its own composition); a subclass config or a consumer-owned instance wins and is never duplicated. One hook, `getDockParticipationConfig()`, returns the consumer's extra seams (`dragEmbodiment`, `hitTest`, the park / conversion seams) and merges under the façade's bindings, the way `getDockProjectionOptions()` merges under the collaborators' options.
3. **The consumers delete their re-derivations.** `VesselWorkspace` declares `dockParticipation: {module: WorkstationParticipation}` and moves its seams into `getDockParticipationConfig()`; `createCrossWindowParticipation`, `refreshCrossWindowParticipation`, `crossWindowParticipationPromise` and the main-workspace handling of `crossWindowParticipations` go. `PopupWorkspace` deletes `syncParticipation`, its `afterSetWindowId` override and the destroy line; reads of `popup.participation` move to the façade's member. Demo B and `examples/dashboard/crossWindowWitness/Harness.mjs:83` stay (not façade consumers). The Institution cockpit inherits the default and publishes no sort group, so its census stays Participation 0 — the negative control.
4. **ADR 0029 §2.3 amendment** under "Dock participation": composition ownership (the façade, under the tear-out lifecycle), the decline rule, the lifecycle triggers, and the unchanged opt-in through `crossWindowSortGroup` — headed `(amendment 2026-10-01, #N)` per the record's convention.

Net lines: the façade grows by the collaborator (~40 lines); the Workstation loses ~90. `Workspace.mjs` sits at 3360 lines; if the reviewer asks for a seam cut, the collaborator composition is the extractable unit, not the façade's bindings.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1 Red-first unit arms in `test/playwright/unit/dashboard/DockWorkspaceParticipation.spec.mjs` (the façade's own spec, the coordinator stub of its sibling): a tear-out workspace that publishes a `crossWindowSortGroup`, holds a `workspaceSet` and receives a `windowId` composes exactly one participation whose target registered once; `dockParticipation: null` composes none; a consumer-supplied instance is kept and not duplicated; a window change unregisters and registers once; `destroy()` unregisters; no published sort group → nothing composed; a published sort group with the lifecycle off still composes.
- [ ] AC-2 `apps/workstation` keeps its behavior with the deletions: `test/playwright/unit/apps/workstation` green; `WorkstationNativePopupOverPopupNL` and `WorkstationHumanPopupOverlapNL` (cross-window drops into main and popups) green headless at the head (their dev reds, if any, named per arm with owners).
- [ ] AC-3 Negative control: the Institution cockpit (tear-out on, no sort group) composes no participation at the head — stated by reading, pinned by a unit arm on a bare tear-out workspace (AC-1's last case).
- [ ] AC-4 ADR 0029 §2.3 carries the amendment paragraph; `learn/` guides that describe the cross-window composition as consumer-owned are swept (`grep -rn "Participation" learn/guides learn/benefits`) and corrected in the same PR.
- [ ] AC-5 Post-merge, outside this PR: the next engine pin in `neomjs/neo-agent-institution` keeps `FleetCockpitTabDragIndicatorsNL` green (the cockpit's drag feedback is `DragAffordances`-composed and unaffected).

## Out of Scope

Demo B's per-host composition and the witness harness (not façade consumers). The in-window affordance tier the cockpit composes by hand (PR neomjs/neo-agent-institution#383 — consumer-owned by the record). Any coordinator change (ADR 0029 §2.3 binding invariant: the coordinator stays dock-blind). The vessel shells of the cockpit becoming dock workspaces.

## Avoided Traps

- Composing the default whether or not a sort group is published: an instance that can never register is a member nobody can observe — the opt-in stays `crossWindowSortGroup`, exactly as the engine class states it.
- A `plugins` entry: `Participation` extends `core.Base`, not `plugin.Base`; forcing it into the plugin list would make `getDockCollaboratorOptions()` (`:1618`) read a surface it does not have.
- Re-registering after every projection: the target's slot is stable by `workspaceId` and ordinary commits retain it (`Workspace.spec.mjs:141`); a per-projection re-sync would churn the coordinator's registry for nothing.

* feat(dock): the Workspace composes its default cross-window Participation for a published sort group (#19350)

The façade owns the participation's lifecycle its own seams already drive: composed once the workspace has a window and publishes a crossWindowSortGroup, kept across unchanged bindings, re-composed on a window change, a set arrival or a host's explicit recompose, destroyed with the workspace. Declinable the maximize way through dockParticipation (true = the lazily imported engine class; {module} = a host subclass; an instance is adopted; null declines); host seams ride getDockParticipationConfig(). The Workstation's main and popup compositions, its participation map and promise, and the per-projection refresh are deleted; the opt-in is the published sort group, not the tear-out flag — the popup workspaces participate with the lifecycle off. ADR 0029 §2.3 carries the amendment.

* test(workstation): the pop-out barriers assert the stable main target instead of a re-creation (#19350)

The façade keeps the main participation across projections, so the three barriers that waited for its id to change after a detach now assert the inverse; the hazard they guarded — a claim landing on a target the refresh was about to destroy — no longer exists.
